entities.name: Niklas Kliesen
entities.description:
Niklas Kliesen was married to genetics researcher Emma Kliesen, and is the father of Leo Kliesen. Niklas is a German archaeologist and spelunker, who also practiced martial arts. He seems to have imparted both hobbies to Leo, and to have been a big influence on them. During a spelunking expedition while Leo was just a child, Niklas went missing and had not been heard from for a time after. Leo vowed to become like Niklas and followed in his footsteps as a professional spelunker.

In reality, Niklas had gone into hiding from the Mishima Zaibatsu to protect the information he gained in his research into the Devil Gene alongside his wife, Emma. After Emma's death at the hands of Kazuya Mishima, Niklas infiltrated G Corporation's Institute for the Study of Prehistoric Civilizations, where Emma's research remained. It was here that Niklas and Leo reunited, as Leo had received a letter from Emma which was scheduled to be sent automatically on the eve of her death, instructing them to find her research at this institute as well.

Niklas was revealed to have been looking into Azazel's connection with the Devil Gene as well as its long history with the Mishima Clan. Following Kazuya Mishima's announcement of the eighth King of Iron Fist Tournament, Niklas and Leo reunite after infiltrating G Corporation's Institute for the Study of Prehistoric Civilizations and recovering Emma Kliesen's research into the Devil Gene.

The pair are approached by Yggdrasil and Lee Chaolan to provide their research into the Devil Gene and Azazel, meeting with Lee, Lars Alexandersson, and Jin Kazama on the flying ship "Víðópnir".

During the end of the second King of Iron Fist Tournament, Nina and Anna underwent Cryogenic Sleep, and on awaking, retained their youthful appearance. While Nina was asleep, she was experimented on by the Mishima Zaibatsu, resulting in her ovum being taken and used to create Steve Fox.

Nina also starred in her own game, Death by Degrees, an action-adventure title released in 2005 for the PlayStation 2.

Nina and her younger sister are from a family of assassins hailing from the Republic of Ireland. Nina was trained in assassination arts by her father and in aikido by her mother. Anna was trained alongside Nina, and the two developed a deadly rivalry, often attempting to humiliate or kill one another.

Nina was contracted to kill Heihachi Mishima at the time of the first King of Iron Fist Tournament. She did not succeed in this task.

Noctis is the crown prince and heir to the throne of the kingdom of Lucis.

Whilst being of aristocratic birth and bearing, Noctis treats his close friends as equals and is often informal with them. He is somewhat reserved and lacks in some social skills due to his isolated childhood upbringing, though is playful and more open with close friends he feels more comfortable around. He can be reckless and egotistical, and worries over others' opinions of him. Ultimately though, he wishes to protect and please his friends and has become more confident in himself.

Noctis is a young man with spiky black hair and blue eyes that can glow red.

Olivia is cheerful and informal whenever she contacts Lars, though it is clear she also respects him and is loyal to him. She rarely seems to take credit, although Lars praises and appreciates her work. She is used to military situations and seems unfazed by them, and is easily able to offer Lars timely warnings when he is in danger.

Olivia appears to be a young woman, possibly in her twenties. She is Caucasian and has short red/ginger hair, her eyes appear to be light in color, and may be blue.

In the Pachislot 4′s Yggdrasil story, Olivia contacts Lars by radio a number of times throughout the mission, and supplies him with information he needs to keep on top of the Mishima Zaibatsu's operations. She frequently warns him of incoming G-Corp and Mishima Zaibatsu enemies who are approaching him. Although she does not make a physical appearance in the game, she is pictured whenever she is on the radio.

Very intelligent, Panda seems to have an almost human-like empathy and thought process. She is shown to be very considerate to Xiaoyu when she is upset, as well as supportive towards her decisions. She sometimes shows a playful side, similar to Xiaoyu.

Panda is often shown rejecting Kuma, sometimes resorting to physical violence as he seeks her out with romantic intent. Although she seems uninterested in Kuma romantically, she does occasionally think of him.

Protector of Ling Xiaoyu. She is cared for at Xiaoyu's high school. To participate in the tournament, Xiaoyu moved to the Mishima Industrial College in Japan. Heihachi Mishima taught Panda advanced bear fighting so that she could act as a bodyguard for Xiaoyu during the tournament. Although Kuma is fond of Panda, she dislikes him and keeps her distance.

Paul Phoenix is a tough American fighter whose battle-spirit was first kindled by his watching 'Bear Killer Willy Williams' as a child. Something of a drifter, Paul had no real career, instead making money by street fighting and taking occasional work as a bouncer while he pursued his real passion: proving himself to be the toughest fighter in the universe. Paul trained with Marshall Law, who would go on to become his good friend, and Lee Chaolan, and remained undefeated in battle until he fought Kazuya Mishima to a draw.

When Paul heard the announcement of the first King of Iron Fist Tournament, he entered, seeing the opportunity to face his rival, Kazuya, and prove himself to be the best. During the tournament, Paul defeated a bear named Kuma, but was unable to defeat Kazuya when they fought.

Two years passed before news reached Paul of a second tournament. Paul entered, and while he was again successful in defeating Kuma, he was still unable to prove himself to be stronger than Kazuya; traffic on the Japanese highways prevented him from reaching the venue in time, forcing him to forfeit.

entities.name: Professor T
entities.description:
Professor T is the head researcher on the forest rejuvenation project known as GENOCELL. His grant for the project came exclusively from G Corporation and the data his research produced was stored on G Corporation supercomputers in a highly secure research base. Julia Chang was one of the researchers on Professor T's team.

The aim of Professor T's research was to study the biological mechanism of reforestation, and to manipulate the cells of plants to grow in arid conditions, thus combatting desertification. The project was a success and GENOCELL was created, an agent that had biological purifying qualities that were able to stimulate biological growth.

Before Julia Chang could apply GENOCELL to her home state of Arizona, however, the Mishima Zaibatsu's Tekken Force raided G Corporation's highly secure labs under the orders of Heihachi Mishima, and stole all GENOCELL data for use in the Zaibatsu's Devil-Human Integration Program. Following the disaster, Professor T informed Julia that their research had been indefinitely halted.

The GENOCELL data seems to have been recovered from the Mishima Zaibatsu by Julia after the 5th King of Iron Fist Tournament, and she was once again working in genetic biology for G Corporation in Tekken 6. It is likely that Professor T was also still an employee of G Corporation at this time, though his team may have been disbanded after it was discovered that Julia was secretly spying on G Corp on behalf of Lee Chaolan's Violet Systems.

entities.name: Prototype Jack
entities.description:
In search of a new, more devastating, weapon, the Russian military began work on the development of androids - superhuman robots built for the purpose of causing destruction. The first step in production was the prototype model of what was to become a line of military robots, which were named "Jack". The prototype was stolen by Heihachi Mishima and his Mishima Zaibatsu, but Russia was still able to produce their main line of Jack robots without the prototype at hand. With the project a success, the first Jack was entered into the King of Iron Fist Tournament. On learning of this, Heihachi entered Prototype Jack into the tournament to face its upgraded counterpart. Prototype Jack was ultimately destroyed by Jack. A couple of years later, the genius Russian scientist, Doctor Bosconovitch, was kidnapped by the new CEO of the Zaibatsu, Kazuya Mishima. Bosconovitch repaired and updated Prototype Jack. After being remodeled and gaining new abilities, Prototype Jack was entered into the second tournament as a rival to the upgraded Jack robot, Jack-2.

It is unknown what happened to Prototype Jack after this. In the non-canonical Tekken Chronicle, some of Prototype Jack's parts, along with parts from Jack and Jack-2, were used in the creation of Gun Jack. Given that Gun Jack inherited some of Prototype Jack's moves, and was partially built in Mishima Industries where Prototype Jack received its upgrades, it is possible that canonically its remains were indeed dismantled and used in the creation of Gun Jack.

Despite being a robot, Prototype Jack was able to develop some kind of sentience. As a result of being discarded in favor of the main Jack series, it came to resent the Jacks and their creators - the Russian government. As a result, Prototype Jack is an aggressive character, determined to grow stronger and smarter in order to destroy all of its opposition, especially the Jacks, which it sees as potentially obsoleting it and jeopardizing its utility. While silent in battle with the exception of generic grunts and growls, outside of battle Prototype Jack was very vocal about its thirst for strength and intelligence, and frequently practices its newly-learned abilities to the point of perfection to ensure it will never again be defeated.

As a prototype model, Prototype Jack's appearance lacks the finesse of the main line of Jacks. In its original appearance, it lacks a human-like torso and arms; its robotic frame is visible and it possesses a pincer and a drill in place of arms. Prototype Jack has a humanoid head, although it is noticeably damaged, and one of its boots is a metal prosthetic. After being remodeled, Prototype Jack gained a new, more distinctive look. It now looks more like the main line of Jack robots, although it lacks the Jacks' skin-like finish; it instead has a shiny, metallic finish. It also now has a rotating hand, a feature which was expanded upon in later releases, allowing it to spin at the waist also.

Raven is a secret intelligence agent who is part of the United Nations’ Raven Unit. He is a subordinate of Master Raven and Victor Chevalier. The Raven Unit was founded when Victor felt the world was on the brink of being taken over by the Mishima Zaibatsu.

Raven was observing Hon-Maru, where members of the Mishima family had been fighting, when G Corporation attacked. Aware that Heihachi Mishima was present in the building when it exploded, Raven reported his supposed death to his unit. He would go on to enter the King of Iron Fist Tournament 5 to gather intel on who was behind the event, given that Heihachi could not have been the one who arranged it.

Later, Raven discovered that Heihachi had survived the explosion at Hon-Maru. They fought briefly, but Raven was ordered back to headquarters and forced to retreat.

entities.name: Reina
entities.description:
Reina is a student attending Mishima Polytechnical School. She understands Heihachi Mishima to be her father.

Reina enrolled at Mishima Polytechnic under the false name of . This falsified information was discovered by Kunimitsu II, who was also enrolled at Mishima Polytechnic as a means to discover more information about the Mishima Zaibatsu under the orders of the United Nations. By some means, Reina was already aware of Kunimitsu's true identity as a thief, and the two initially clashed as this information came to light. Having each tested the other's strength in this confrontation, the two came to an agreement to use one another to their own individual benefit, while acting as best friends on the surface.

Several months before the announcement of the eigth King of Iron Fist Tournament, Reina approached Kunimitsu to propose a deal: she would provide Kunimitsu with intel on the location of nine ancient blades known as the Kuatatou that were once used by an ancient head of the Mishima Clan to seal away demons, and Kunimitsu in turn would provide Reina with information on G Corporation's forces. Kunimitsu agreed, and upon finding said blades, provided Reina with confidential intel on G Corporation's upcoming attempt to occupy New York.

After acquiring this information, Reina shared it with Lidia Sobieska, who alerted her allies in Yggdrasil. Lidia later met with Reina, who put her on the trail of the Tekken Monks, an organization who had been thwarting attempts to locate the missing Heihachi Mishima.

entities.description:
Revenant was an exclusive non-playable character and antagonist introduced in Tekken (Mobile). He is the final boss of the game.

Revenant appears during Kazuya and Nina's match, and steals their power via a huge black sphere. Kazuya and Nina join forces and recruit other fighters to defeat Revenant, and take back their power. Revenant uses fighters known as Acolytes, who were under his mind control, to battle them.

After Revenant was defeated, he summoned Ogre, proclaiming that all the power he collected is now Ogre's. After being released from its giant sphere, Ogre, who was impressed by the strength of the fighters wanted them to join him, but they refused Ogre's offer and promised to fight him. With that, Revenant warns the fighters that they are no match for them before disappearing in shadowed light.

Revenant relies on charging himself to hit his opponent in massive damage depending on using both basic or special moves.

entities.name: Richard Williams
entities.description:
Richard Williams worked as an assassin for the Irish Republican Army. He retired to marry a British Aikido champion and the two lived in the Republic of Ireland, where they had two daughters. Both daughters were raised to know both their father's assassination techniques and their mother's aikido. The elder daughter, Nina Williams, had an aptitude for Richard's art that meant he favored her. His younger daughter, Anna Williams, craved his attention and affection, but was of little interest to him as she was more reluctant to become an assassin. Richard expected both his daughters to continue on the family business as assassins-for-hire. He may have been involved in sending Nina off for experiments in emotional repression when she was young. His favoring of Nina over Anna begun a lifelong rivalry between the two which has not yet been resolved.

Richard died, likely of natural causes, around the time of the second King of Iron Fist Tournament, in 1996. Both his daughters held a temporary truce when they visited his grave.

From the way his daughters regard him, Richard seems to have been an aloof and hard-to-please individual, more like his daughter Nina than Anna. He openly favored Nina over Anna and pressured both into following in his footsteps to be assassins. In a tweet, Katsuhiro Harada revealed that, failing to impress Richard with her martial arts, Anna took up cooking in order to show her father she was good at something Nina was not. Richard told her such an endeavour was pointless as it did not further the family status as assassins.

In the main Tekken series, Richard's appearance is never specified or referenced. He appears however in the spin-off game Death by Degrees, in which he is depicted with receding auburn hair and a close beard and moustache.

Rippers are enemies that appear in the Tekken spin-off game, Death By Degrees. They are cyborgs created by the criminal organization Kometa. Nina encounters them aboard the Amphitrite, facing several models equipped with various weaponry.

Rippers are tall, humanoid cyborgs adorned with robotic and metal components. They wear combat trousers and boots. Some versions of the Ripper feature additional weaponry and armor, such as cannons, flamethrowers and large Ripper blades. The indication that they used to possibly be human is their pale white torso shown.

The Rippers were developed by Kometa, a criminal organization specializing in weapon modification and smuggling. Lana Lei would acquire cadavers from the fighting tournaments she would host on the Amphitrite including the executives killed by Enrique Ortega.

Upon her return to the Amphitrite, Nina will face many Rippers as she tracks down Lana. She eventually learns from Alan that she herself was a potential subject to be "converted" into a cyborg too.

entities.description:
An alternate version of himself named Slim Bob is playable in Tekken Tag Tournament 2. As the name suggests, he is a skinny version of Bob which first made an appearance in Bob's Tekken 6 ending.

Robert 'Bob' Richards was heralded as a master of martial arts from a young age, with a past as a bail bondsman. He garnered many fans with his chiseled body and good looks. However, he could not defeat opponents who were larger than him. He vanished from the martial arts scene to pursue a special training regimen that increased his power and weight whilst maintaining his agility.

After several years of seclusion, Bob returned to the scene, having gained a large amount of weight. Bob paid no attention to critics of his changed body, confident in the mixture of speed, power, and weight his regimen had imbued him with. Deciding that he was ready to return to competition, he entered the King of Iron Fist Tournament 6.

After the cancellation of the sixth King of Iron Fist Tournament, Bob intended to enter the seventh, but was stopped by Bryan Fury, who was in the midst of a violent rampage. In his attempt to stop the cyborg, Bob was injured when the road beneath he and Bryan collapsed, leaving Bob hospitalized.

entities.name: Roger
entities.description:
Roger is a genetically engineered kangaroo with the ability to fight, jump extremely high and run very fast. He was the first kangaroo born at the Mishima Zaibatsu's biotech labs as part of Kazuya Mishima's program to create transgenic military animals. The program was run by Mishima Industries and headed by Doctor Bosconovitch. Kazuya later deemed this experiment to be a useless failure.

Roger was entered into the King of Iron Fist Tournament 2 as a competitor. Shortly after this, he met his wife and the two had a joey that they named Roger Jr.. The three lived in peace, having apparently escaped the labs after Kazuya's fall from power. Many years later, however, Roger was kidnapped. It is not clear who he was kidnapped by, but he ended up back in the destroyed Zaibatsu laboratories that had belonged to Dr Bosconovitch. He remained here however of his own volition, living in luxury, until his wife and son found him. Deeply disappointed by his abandoning them, Roger's Wife divorced him. It is unclear what happened to Roger after this, although in the non-canon Tekken Tag Tournament 2 he is remorseful of his actions and seeks out his family to try and apologize to them.

Version 1: When Kazuya built his private military force, he didn't have his sight set on only humans, but also animals too, and thus the development of animals for military use moved forward. The research team for the development of animals for military use conducted tests using drugs and DNA manipulation. And as a result, Roger, came to have more mobility than the usual kangaroo; he jumped 23-meters on one occasion, and ran as fast as 60km/h.

Since the announcement of the martial arts tournament, Roger continuously waits for anything to mistakenly enter his territory in order to obliterate it.

One day, Roger was kidnapped, and his wife and son left to try and find him. They discovered him living in luxury however, uncaring of their fate, and Roger's Wife decided to divorce him. Now Roger Jr. and his mother live alone and try to make ends meet by fighting together in tournaments.

Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection Manual, PAL Roger Jr. is part of a second generation of kangaroos that were genetically altered and bred for military use. After the disappearance of his father, Roger Jr. decided to enter the tournament, hoping it would provide clues to his father's whereabouts.

One day Roger was kidnapped and taken away. His wife and son joined the fifth King of Iron Fist tournament to find Roger.

Roger's Wife and Roger Jr. found Roger, but he turned out to be living a life of luxury, unconcerned about his family. Roger's wife decided to divorce him and raise her son on her own. Life became financially difficult for them and they decided to enter the sixth King of Iron Fist Tournament for the money.

"Regarding 'SAKE', this was included when we planned to implement a new animal character. But there were a few problems..."

"It was really a salmon so, no matter if you press punch or kick, the character just flops around making a flapping noise... At the time, one play was 100 yen (a little over a dollar) so that is the quality bar to keep in mind for customer satisfaction. So we thought players would get quite angry if they had to pay that much to play such a character, and we gave up on that character. That kind of character might be OK in a console version, but not for the arcade."

Salim was described as 'bright and full of knowledge'. He and Shaheen had a mutual respect for one another and were dedicated to their principles, including protecting the wealth and pride of others. Salim's brother, Zarif, believes that Salim was killed for standing up to G Corporation's tyranny and refusing to grant them access to his company's oil.

Salim came from a wealthy and prominent family in Saudi Arabia, where he was cherished by his family. He had one younger brother Zarif, who is also dedicated to him.

One day, thirteen years ago, Salim was the target of an assassination attempt. He was saved by a boy his own age who had been trained in fighting. This was his first meeting with Shaheen. Salim took Shaheen's hands and told him "You should use such skills to become a shield for those in need." He welcomed Shaheen as a bodyguard for him. Salim's family, delighted that Shaheen had saved their son, were happy to take him under their wing.

Later, the two friends went their separate ways, though both were dedicated to protecting the wealth and pride of others. Salim became the head of an oil company, and Shaheen a private military specialist.

entities.description:
Unlike his employer, Mr. de Rochefort, Sebastian seems to approve of Lili's desire to fight, as seen in her Tekken Tag Tournament 2 ending, and seems to have even adopted her fighting style. Him being able to fight and move the same as Lili could be considered non-canon, however, as it is seen only in the aforementioned non-canon game.

Sebastian appears to be a kind and caring man. He is always happy and positive for Lili's accomplishments, as seen in Lili's Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection ending when he congratulates her for winning the tournament, crying with joy for her. He also seems to equate Lili’s fights with and teasing of Asuka as her "making friends" and showing affection. Nevertheless, he always loyally assists Lili in her antics, either at her side directly or via calls.

Not much is known about Sebastian. His only line in Lili's ending is; "Truly splendid, Miss Lili.", to which Lili replies; "Sebastian, you're too much. I only did what any daughter would do". What Sebastian and Lili do not realize is that Rochefort Enterprises is now bankrupt.

Sebastian makes an appearance in Lili's ending where, after she and Asuka get into a fight, he happily comments that Lili is already making friends.

entities.description:
Seiryu is a powerful martial artist committed to the revival of the lost arts of the Tekken Monks. He personally saved Heihachi Mishima from falling into lava after his battle with Kazuya Mishima. Seiryu believed in the possibility of redeeming Heihachi, should Heihachi's memories remain locked away. He speaks in older, formal Japanese.

Seiryu is a severe martial artist, and devoted to the old way of Mishima Style Fighting Karate.

Seiryu is bald and tan, like Suzaku, but possesses a musculature rivaling Heihachi Mishima and is taller than him by a head. He also wears a monk uniform similar to Suzaku's and Heihachi's during the latter's six-month training at Genmaji Temple. He is topless, barefoot, and wears fist-size Buddhist prayer beads, each etched with "拳" (Ken), around his neck.

Seiryu wears his respective Tekken High Priest Azure Dragon mask, but conforms his fashion towards a warrior Buddhist monk. His pants display colors and patterns related to the Azure Dragon totem.

entities.description:
Dragunov is a member of the Spetsnaz (also known as the Russian Special Operatives) who have dubbed him "The White Angel of Death" and "White Reaper" due to his overwhelming fighting powers and inscrutable personality.

Dragunov is a member of an elite special operations unit in the Russian military. This role has put him in conflict with parties including the United Nations officers Raven and Master Raven, and earned him the moniker "The White Angel of Death".

He was sent to the King of Iron Fist Tournament 5 on a clandestine mission to capture a specimen of interest to the Russian military, but failed to secure the organism. On his return to Russia, Dragunov was deployed to quell the civil unrest spreading through the country due to the actions of covert Mishima Zaibatsu operatives. Dragunov was withdrawn from this mission and redeployed to infiltrate the King of Iron Fist Tournament 6 and take down the Mishima Zaibatsu. The outcome of this mission is not stated.

He would later enter the King of Iron Fist Tournament 7 on army orders. After this, Dragunov was permitted to take extended leave for the first time in his life. He took this opportunity to review his personal bucket list and settled on trying to complete a particularly difficult task.

entities.name: Shaheen
entities.description:
Shaheen (Arabic: شاهين Shahin, Japanese: シャヒーン Shahīn) is a character in the Tekken series who was introduced in Tekken 7 as one of the new playable characters.

Shaheen learned the art of fighting from a young age from his father. One day, thirteen years ago, Shaheen saved a boy his own age from an assassination attempt. This boy, Salim, would become his lifelong best friend.

After being saved, Salim told Shaheen he should used his skills to protect others. He took Shaheen by the hands and asked him to be a bodyguard for him. Shaheen was welcomed into Salim's household, who were a prominant family in the local area.

Salim and Shaheen eventually went their separate ways when they grew older. Shaheen enrolled in the army, where he was noted for his ability in one-on-one combat, and later became a member of a private military firm, specializing in the provision of security services. Salim, meanwhile, took over his family's oil company.

entities.name: Shin Kamiya
entities.description:
is a character exclusive to the Tekken: Blood Vengeance movie.

Shin is a young Japanese man with a bandage wrapped around his whole left arm. He wears black pants and sneakers with white soles and a white short-sleeved button-up shirt. With his M-Cell activated, Shin is shirtless with green glowing veins but remains with the pants and shoes. Without the M-Cell, Shin has a black tattoo on his left arm, similar to the Devil Gene tattoo.

Shin was a young Japanese student and an old friend of Jin Kazama, who went to Mishima Polytechnic School with him. In Blood Vengeance, both the Mishima Zaibatsu and G Corporation are looking for information about him in order to track down Shin himself. So Alisa Bosconovitch (under the orders of Nina Williams) and Ling Xiaoyu (under the orders of Anna Williams) are sent to spy on him at his school in Kyoto.

During their investigation, Alisa and Xiaoyu team up with each other and work together, and Xiaoyu herself turns against Anna. At that moment, Shin is kidnapped by an unknown assailant. Later on, the two girls learn more about Shin's background and soon discover that genetic experiments were being done on Shin and his classmates (who were presumably other friends of Jin), and now realize that the Mishimas were seeking Shin, who is in fact the sole survivor of his classmates and M Cell subject, for immortality.

entities.name: Silver Fighting God
entities.description:
The is the second known creature in the Tekken series belonging to the classification of . It was introduced in Tekken 8 with the addition of new character Miary Zo, and appears to be a benevolent being worshiped as a deity by the people of Madagascar.

Unlike its predecessor, Ancient Ogre, the Silver Fighting God is seen as benevolent. It is not known to harm humans, and is instead treated as a deity of protection.

The Silver Fighting God has a bestial form similar to that of True Ogre. It is bipedal, with reptilian, clawed feet and digitigrade legs wrapped at the ankles with tattered white cloth. Its face resembles that of a lion, with bony growths along the jaw and the sides of the head, and surrounding a single, pointed, twisting horn coming from the center of its forehead. It has a large silver mane around its head and chest, and large white feathered wings speckled with black near the tips. The Silver Fighting God also has the tail of a lemur, with black and white stripes. The underside of this tail appears to be scaled, as does the skin on the rest of its body. The exposed skin of the Silver Fighting God also bears glowing, blue symbols, seen across its torso, arms, legs, and tail.

While the Silver Fighting God's left arm is clawed with more bone-like growths coming from the elbow, its right arm is mostly humanoid until the elbow, where it transitions into multiple snakes. The Silver Fighting God wears a tattered loincloth around its waist, a band around its left thigh, white cloth around its left wrist, and multiple white necklaces.

entities.name: Slim Bob
entities.description:
Slim Bob has curly blond hair and blue eyes. In Bob's Tekken 6 ending, he shares the same facial hair as his larger counterpart, but as a playable character in Tekken Tag Tournament 2, Slim Bob's face is clean shaven. He has a slim figure, as his name would suggest.

Ending Description: Bob became famous after winning The King of the Iron Fist Tournament 6. He was seemingly showered with never-ending popularity, with interviews that came day or night. Without noticing, he becomes slimmer. The Slim Bob is shown in a weight-room measuring his weight. Only reaching around 70kg (154 lbs), he becomes frustrated. Unsatisfied with the results, he steps back on. The scale has the same results. Even more infuriated, he starts to beat his head against the wall, then becomes exhausted and lies down.

Slim Bob is featured as a DLC character in the console version of Tekken Tag Tournament 2.

Profile: With the dream of becoming a gifted fighter, Bob was popular among his fans for his handsome looks. His tournaments were always sold out, and his popularity was skyrocketing to the top...and yet he still was unsatisfied.

entities.name: Soul Sphere
entities.description:
The Soul Sphere is the second final boss in Tekken 5′s Devil Within. It also serves as the fourth boss in Stage 4 of the Ruins.

The Soul Sphere is an orb of light, having a mix of purple, blue, and white on it. Its core is pure white, while its energy around it consists of a mix of lighter shades of purple and blue. But once it acts up, it violently bursts into a ball of electricity, consisting of purple.

Before the battle starts, the Soul Sphere stays in one place. Once it detects Jin Kazama, it violently bursts into a ball of electricity.

In battle, the first thing the Soul Sphere does is to hover around and then bump into Jin. If the player dodges the Soul Sphere or gets hit by it, the sphere will summon warriors that were once the Tekken Force. After defeating the warriors, the sphere will attempt to bump into Jin again. While it misses or succeeds, the Soul Sphere will open up one of the barriers of its generators. These generators are almost similar to one oft he door generators in Stage 4 and 5, but having a smooth gray brick texture, purple outlines, and a blue aura underneath. If the Soul Sphere affects one of the generators, it'll summon balls of energy that look similar to the sphere itself. The player must destroy this generator, or else they will have to repeat the first phase. Once the generator has been destroyed, the platform it stands on will fade away, and then the player will engage the second phase.

entities.name: Steve Fox
entities.description:
With his debut in Tekken 4, it was revealed that he is the biological son of Nina Williams and an unnamed legendary boxer that his conception was carried out synthetically by the Mishima Zaibatsu. Then later in Tekken Tag Tournament 2 and Tekken 7, it was revealed that the Zaibatsu ordered his conception in order to get themselves a new, more durable, test subject for their experiments.

Steve Fox is a boxer who was created by the Mishima Zaibatsu. After reclaiming the Mishima Zaibatsu from his son and witnessing the power of the Devil firsthand in the second King of Iron Fist Tournament, CEO Heihachi Mishima began his own research into the terrifying power of the Devil Gene. In an attempt to replicate this superhuman strength, the Mishima Zaibatsu started a genetic modification plan with the goal of replicating the effects of the gene on regular humans through the creation of a synthetic Devil Gene. Heihachi used eggs from the assassin Nina Williams, who was cryogenically frozen by Doctor Bosconovitch at the Zaibatsu at the time, to create babies that he used to conduct these experiments. Most of the children died as a result of the experiments and the supersoldier program was ultimately considered a failure.

One of the children in the program was known as Subject NT01, or Steve. A doctor supervising the experimentation on Steve, Emma Kliesen, developed a bond with the boy, much to the disparagement of her more clinically minded colleagues. It was also Emma who helped Steve escape the laboratories at the age of six by faking his death in an experiment. At some point following this, it is likely that Steve was adopted and subsequently raised in the United Kingdom. It is unknown to what extent the childhood experiments affected Steve's physical capabilities. Regardless, by the age of 21, Steve Fox was a middleweight boxing champion. Steve remembered very little about his early childhood, and his driving motivations prior to his King of Iron Fist Tournament debut were to find out who his birth parents were and to discover how he got the large scar on his left arm.

Steve entered the King of Iron Fist Tournament 4 after becoming embroiled in trouble with The Syndicate. Despite the danger, Steve believed the tournament would bolster his chances of connecting with his birth parents. At the tournament, he met Lei Wulong, who was able to help Steve discover that he was created by the Mishima Zaibatsu.

entities.description:
Sugar is a minor character in the Tekken series. She is Leroy Smith's pet dog who first appeared in Tekken 7: Fated Retribution as part of Leroy's move set and win poses.

Sugar is an American Bully, a pit bull-type dog. Sugar is the pet of Leroy Smith and accompanies her master during battle. Leroy can summon Sugar into combat, but the dog will only attack randomly.

Sugar appears at Leroy's side during his entry to the third King of Iron Fist Tournament and remains with him during and after his defeat at the hands of Jin Kazama. Although she is initially aggressive towards Jin due to his fight with her master, Leroy reassures her that his opponent is no enemy.

entities.name: Super Combot DX
entities.description:
Super Combot DX is a robot in the Tekken series of fighting games. It is only playable in Tekken Tag Tournament 2, though makes an appearance in a Tekken 7 stage, meaning the robot does canonically exist. Super Combot DX is the improved version of Combot, created by the company Violet Systems.

In Combot's biography in Tekken Tag Tournament 2, it is explained that due to public humiliation caused by unexpected failures in battle by Combot in the fourth tournament, Violet swore revenge. To do this Violet created a new model of Combot: Super Combot DX whose design mobilized all the resources of Violet Systems.

See Fight Lab In the lab, when everything is ready to start, Violet, when activating Super Combot DX, hits the wrong button. The Super Combot DX and most of the lab are blown up. Thus Violet must take an old Combot model, and go through all the training again. At the end of Fight Lab, the Super Combot DX is ready again and it proceeds to defeat Heihachi, Kazuya, and Jin, until Devil Jin blasts its head off with a laser. Lee remarks that he's forgotten to input devil data into the bot, but says nevermind, and proceeds to activate Super Combot's self-destruct sequence, detonating it and his family with it.

entities.name: Suzaku
entities.description:
An elderly man with great patience and open-mindedness. He speaks in elderly-style, formal Japanese.

Suzaku is bald and tan, like Seiryu, but possesses a thinner musculature and wears the complete traditional Tekken Monks attire.

Suzaku wears his respective Tekken High Priest Vermilion Bird mask, the Tekken Monk's robe, and a conical hat. His pants display colors and patterns related to the Vermilion Bird totem.

As the lead priest of the Tekken Monks, he aims to put the Mishima Style Fighting Karate on a right and just path. After Seiryu had just barely saved Heihachi Mishima from falling into the lava following his bout with Kazuya, Suzaku sends a group of monks to test Lidia Sobieska in battle. After Lidia bests Seiryu, Suzaku summons Shadow Kazuya to fight her to see if she fights for justice.

Taekwondo Girl is a character who was set to appear in Tekken (Mobile) as a fighter. Due to the announcement of the game's shutdown on February 15, 2019, she will no longer be released and is now a cancelled character.

Taekwondo Girl is a young woman with long black hair, fair skin, and brown eyes. She wears a blue and white sportswear jacket that reveals part of her chest and belly. The sleeves are raised and a white fox with nine tails is represented on the front of the jacket. Her gloves and pants are also blue and white. She also sports a black belt which has written in white, "Nine Tailed Fox."

The , is the private corporate army of the Mishima Zaibatsu, featured in the Tekken fighting game series. They first appeared in Tekken 3. They were built up by Heihachi Mishima who greatly expanded the military capacity of the Zaibatsu after he retook the corporation from his son, Kazuya Mishima.

The Tekken Force motto (or at least the motto of the Special Forces Operational Group) is Potius mori quam tradere - 'It is better to die, than to betray'.

At the beginning of Tekken 6 the size of Tekken Force was just under 60,000 soldiers. Lars Alexandersson states that he led over half of Tekken Force's soldiers into rebellion, and one of Heihachi Mishima's bodyguards in Tekken 6 informs Heihachi that Lars's rebel army consists of around 30,000 soldiers, making the approximate total number of Tekken Force units prior to desertion at this time just under 60,000. As well as Lars's forces which seceded from Tekken Force before the start of Tekken 6, a number of special forces also left Jin's Tekken Force in order to join Heihachi and remained loyal to him rather than Jin.

entities.name: Tekken Monks
entities.description:
The are an order of warrior monks featured in the Tekken fighting game series. They practice an old form of Mishima Style Fighting Karate, and first appeared in Tekken 8 Season 1 Pass DLC.

The Tekken Monks' foundation was previously unknown, kept secret by its members for many centuries. Their existence became known six months ago, during the height of the war between G Corporation and the Mishima Zaibatsu. The order began taking out the remnants of the Mishima Zaibatsu after Heihachi Mishima disappeared and Nina Williams left. While initially suspected to have a connection with G Corporation, the monks' true motives are unknown.

It is revealed that the Tekken Monks' origin occurred when two clans, warring over who was to be the successor of the Mishima Style Fighting Karate, fought. The losing clan retreated to follow Buddhist principles and seek to stay true to the 'pure' style of the Mishima Style - this was the time when they became known as the Tekken Monks. As a result, the monks have had an unfavorable stance on the Mishima Clan and their Zaibatsu. Despite this, the monks decided to go out of their way to save Heihachi, apparently standing close by during his fight with Kazuya, and rescuing him before he was thrown into lava. Since Heihachi was amnesiac, they believed this was an opportunity to set Heihachi on the right path.

After testing Heihachi, with the aid of Lidia Sobieska, the monks believed Heihachi to be of sound body, mind, and spirit, and taught him their 'Star Crusher' technique, in time for him to utilize this power against an asteroid, said to fall to Earth every 200 years. While destroying this asteroid, Heihachi headbutted it - the jolt he needed (and the technique used often in his old fighting style against his sons) to regain his memories.

To pick Tetsujin in Arcade mode, one must go all the way to the left on the bottom row of characters. Tetsujin/Mokujin will be in the invisible box to the left of Wang.

Given that Ogre, Devil and Unknown are present in Tekken Tag Tournament, it is assumed that Mokujin arose again to stop them. Seeing as there are three evil forces to be stopped, this may explain why Tetsujin was also "activated".

Ending Description: Tetsujin's ending is the same as Mokujin's, where Tetsujin is training and performing kata with multiple other, wooden Mokujins in unison. The ending still takes place on the Law-B stage.

Tetsujin returns, for the first time since Tekken Tag Tournament, as the second strongest sub-boss in the game. He plays the same as Mokujin, but gives more rewards, though not as much as Kinjin.

entities.name: The Journalist
entities.description:
The Journalist acts as the narrator of the Tekken 7: Fated Retribution Story Mode. The unnamed journalist was originally a war correspondent, reporting on the war between the Mishima Zaibatsu and G Corporation. He lost his family due to the destruction of a city in the war started by Jin Kazama. The Journalist seeks to research the Mishima Clan during the events of the King of Iron Fist Tournament 7.

The Journalist is a caucasian man with short brown hair, a stubble beard and moustache, and glasses. His full face and eyes are never shown, with all shots of him being angled away, or cast in heavy light or shadow. He usually wears an informal suit, with an unbuttoned shirt, sometimes with a vest and jacket. During his time as a war correspondent, he can be seen in an armored vest with 'PRESS' written on the back and a helmet.

After the destruction of his home, the Journalist begins his research on the Mishimas whilst living in a small hotel room. Seeking to know the answers behind the prolonged conflict, the Journalist begins by learning about the Zaibatsu's origins as an armaments manufacturer under Jinpachi Mishima, and the company's more peaceful route taken after World War Two. He learns about Heihachi Mishima's coup to take the company from his father, and that in the same year, Heihachi killed his wife Kazumi Mishima (née Hachijo), and threw his young son, Kazuya Mishima, off a cliff. The Journalist is later approached by Lee Chaolan, who tells him more about the Mishima family, and introduces him to Lars Alexandersson.

On seeing Jin's recovered body at a Violet Systems facility, The Journalist considers killing him, but is prevented from doing so by Lars. Lars tells him that, although he understands his reasons, he needs Jin to live so that he can stop the war he started. The Journalist is with Lars, Lee and Alisa Bosconovitch when the Mishima Zaibatsu broadcasts footage of Kazuya in his devil form. An Orbital Satellite then destroys G Corporation's Millennium Tower, and, at some point afterwards, Kazuya shoots down the satellite in retaliation. An unknown source claims that the Mishima Zaibatsu are responsible for their own satellite falling out of orbit, and the subsequent destruction as it falls to earth turns public opinion against the Zaibatsu.

entities.description:
The thug is a nameless young man that appears in two fighter endings in Tekken 6.

The thug is depicted a tan, lanky, Caucasian man who covers his body in brown tribal tattoos, face piercings, and wears his hair in a red or pink Mohawk.

He wears a blue jersey top with white trim that has a white "9" in a white ring on the front, and a cartoony skeleton on the back. His pants are black, and his wristbands are dark brown with silver studs. He also wears a silver chain necklace, and in Anna's ending, a pair of thin black sunglasses.

He first appears in Anna Williams's ending. When she and Nina play billiards, she bumps her bottom against his by mistake, turning around to apologize before accidentally hitting him with her cue stick. The thug is not happy about this, as he takes out a knife and is ready to attack her. Anna and Nina retaliate, are victorious over him, and Lee Chaolan, who serves as the bartender, gives them an "excellent" thumbs-up, much to Nina's surprise.

entities.description:
Tiger is a mysterious man who entered the "The King of Iron Fist Tournament" dressed in clothes inspired by the golden ages of soul and disco music. His polished capoeira moves look quite similar to those used by Eddy Gordo, but the nature of the relationship between these two fighters remains a mystery.

Though Tiger never speaks, he is depicted in the games as fun-loving and carefree, dancing in his intros, outros, and Arcade Mode endings.

Tiger is a dark-skinned man whose hair in each of his appearances is always styled in an afro. In his Tekken Tag Tournament render, his eyes are shown to be brown. In Tekken 3 and Tekken Tag Tournament, Tiger has full sideburns with a moustache, while in his Tekken Tag Tournament 2 appearance, his sideburns are paired with a neatly-trimmed goatee.

Tiger does not have an official storyline within Tekken 3.

entities.description:
Tiger Miyagi was a freely playable character in Tekken (Mobile) before the app closed.

Tiger's special moves were a blend between Kazuya and Jin's moves. He could utilize Jin's Thrusting Uppercut and his Demon's Paw as well as Heihachi and Jinpachi's Hell Axle.

Tiger Miyagi used the traditional Karate which originated in modern-day Okinawa (formerly the Ryukyu Kingdom). His main style, however, was a blend between Jin's traditional karate based on Kyokushin and Kazuya's Advanced Mishima Style Fighting Karate based on Shotokan.

entities.name: Tougou
entities.description:
Tougou is calm and level-headed, and used to taking on a leadership role. He easily assumes command when Lars is amnesiac, and according to a conversation between him and Lars in Scenario Campaign, often takes over leading troops so that Lars can become a frontline fighter and do some damage. He is tactically minded and loyal to Lars. He has a sense of honor and believes that the cause he fights for is more important than himself and his own well-being.

Tougou has short, brown hair, brown eyes, and a stubble beard. He has a long scar running down the right side of his face, from his brow to just under his cheek bone. He wears Yggdrasil armor (modified Tekken Force armor), with one pauldron larger than the other, and carries a sword.

Tougou plays an important role in the Tekken 6 story. He is the second-in-command of Yggdrasil, the rebel army that Lars Alexandersson leads, who are a splinter of Tekken Force that defected in the face of Jin Kazama's warmongering direction for the Mishima Zaibatsu. Tougou first enters the story looking for Lars after an Yggdrasil raid on a Zaibatsu laboratory went wrong. Lars's group was attacked by a simultaneous raid done by G Corporation, resulting in the elimination of almost their whole squadron. Whilst searching for survivors, Tougou was forced to pull troops out of the lab as the army were on their way. Tougou later discovered that Lars was alive, but was dismayed to find a head concussion had left Lars amnesiac and unaware of who he was or the cause he was fighting for. Undaunted by this, Tougou supported Lars by providing him with remote intelligence and leading Yggdrasil in his absence, until Lars was ready to return.

As Lars sought to regain his memories, Tougou provided intelligence on such factors as the Zaibatsu's raid on Ogre's temple, including the whereabouts of an associated epitaph that he found in an underground facility beneath the Zaibatsu Headquarters, and encouraged Lars to seek out Heihachi Mishima, with whom he had unfinished business. This last encounter prompted Lars to remember his heritage and the rest of his forgotten memories, and, thereafter, he, Alisa Bosconovitch, and Tougou work together more closely, launching Yggdrasil raids against the Mishima Zaibatsu and G Corporation.

entities.name: True Ogre
entities.description:
True Ogre, also referred to simply as Ogre, is a fictional character and villain in the Tekken series. It is the final boss of Tekken 3 and Tekken Card Challenge, and the sub-boss of Tekken Tag Tournament 2. It is the final canonical transformation of Ancient Ogre.

Unlike its first form which speaks and seems to be a being of intelligence, True Ogre is more of a howling beast. It loses its ability to speak and instead roars and just attacks and absorbs the powers of those that come to confront it. True Ogre behaves like a wild beast, as shown in its throw moves and in its special continue screen when it is the boss fight in Tekken Tag Tournament 2. In the continue screen, it appears to devour the defeated player character.

Ogre's second form stands not much taller than its first, but is hunched over to an extent. In this incarnation, it resembles more a monster than a human, with a large frame, dark brown fur, a monstrous face, a tail, wings, horns and snakes in place of a right arm. All of the jewelry Ogre wore in its previous form disappear, save for one leg armlet. Also, in this form, the area surrounding it will dim to an eerie pitch black (in Tekken 3), or extremely dark (in the arcade version of Tekken Tag Tournament).

True Ogre has no outfits as such; instead, its colors vary between "outfits" and there are slight alterations to its appearance.

entities.name: Type J
entities.description:
Type J were robots created by Doctor Bosconovitch, developed for the criminal organization Kometa. They serve as antagonists in the Tekken spin-off game Death by Degrees.

The original robot is located at the Solitaria Penitentiary. Three of the robots are located on the Amphitrite. They are named "J Robots" because the letter "J" is inscribed on their abdomens. These robots are concealed in cases. These cases are unlocked with the non-contact type IC key that has the letter "J" inscribed on the handle, with the exception of the first Type J, which can exit the case on its own.

The Type J robots are massive robots several times taller than a human. Two robots somewhat resemble a four-legged animal like a dog or lion, the other two can also stand on two legs like a human. Their heads are humanoid, with red glowing eyes and a metal 'halo' around the crown of their heads.

The first Type J is a dark grey color. It is equipped with two claws and has a quadrupedal and bipedal mode. This type J has the ability to climb on the walls and ceilings, and is also equipped with a flamethrower on it's mouth and a cannon that shoots shuriken-like projectiles. They also explode once they track Nina with red lasers.

entities.name: Unknown
entities.description:
This page is about the character. For the stage with the same name, see Unknown (Stage).

Little is known of Unknown's origins, yet it seems as though a creature resembling a Wolf Spirit possessed her for its own purpose, which is to complete itself, as shown in Unknown's Tekken Tag Tournament ending. The creature accompanies her in battle and mimics Unknown's moves and actions, possibly as it controls her actions.

Unknown returns in Tekken Tag Tournament 2, this time without the Wolf Spirit, implying that she was able to escape the spirits control at the end of the first Tag Tournament.

Since Tekken Tag Tournaments release, Namco has not provided any clear explanation on Unknown. The comic book Tekken Forever was meant to explain who Unknown was, but it was canceled after only one issue. A Limited Edition version of Tekken 6 was released in September 2009, and an artbook which was part of the package revealed that Unknown was originally supposed to be Jun Kazama's sister by the name of , but this story arc was dropped when Tekken Tag Tournament became a non-canon spin-off game.

entities.name: Victor Chevalier
entities.description:
Victor is the leader and founder of the United Nations' independent forces. He also founded and trained the Raven Unit.

Victor is a refined, suave man of elegance from an aristocratic background. He has been motivated ever since childhood by a desire to save those in need. He is thrifty and enjoys dalliances in romance, and is described as having broken many hearts. From his voice lines, he appears to be someone with immeasurable self-confidence and no small degree of arrogance. He is a tactically minded man, observing the trends of global politics and corporate rises in power and setting out to challenge these threats. This is also attested to by one of his in-fight voice lines: "Checkmate". Victor is also fascinated with Japanese culture thanks to his stay with his father's mercenary friend in Japan.

Victor is an older man with gray hair brushed back and side-parted, and a gray mustache and beard. He has blue eyes and black eyebrows. He appears to be lean, and to favor elegant clothing, wearing a three-piece suit. He has many technological gadgets, including on his sunglasses and utilizes high tech weapons.

Abridged Profile Victor Chevalier is a living legend who founded the UN’s independent forces. Descended from a lineage of distinguished knights, with a dream to rescue those in need. He followed the footsteps of his father and enlisted in the French Navy before joining the UN following his will to save more people.

entities.name: Violet
entities.description:
The persona 'Violet' was created by Lee Chaolan some time between the events of Tekken 2 and Tekken 4. He used this identity to hide from his father, Heihachi Mishima, and was eventually able to build up his own robotics company, based in The Bahamas. Violet is the official CEO of Violet Systems, and, initially, the name Lee Chaolan was completely dissociated from the company. As well as being CEO of his company, Violet is also its foremost roboticist, undertaking much of the engineering work personally himself.

In the King of Iron Fist Tournament 4, Lee entered as his alter-ego Violet, and also entered Combot as a competitor, in order to show off its abilities. He was shocked to find his brother, Kazuya Mishima, alive and lost to him as a consequence. Kazuya seems to have instantly seen through Lee's disguise, and thereafter, Lee hasn't particularly troubled to hide himself as Violet. He does still occasionally dress in this persona however, and his company is still registered under this name.

When in his persona as Violet, Lee seems to distance himself from Mishima affairs, and puts on more of a reckless playboy air instead of the more gallant and romantic air he has as Lee Chaolan. Lee will show a more classical and refined image of himself, while Violet is a bit more excited or even sometimes rude as seen in some of his replies in Tekken Supporters, and he likes to tease his secretary, as seen in Fight Lab. With the way he dismisses his secretary’s criticism and always tries to relax and enjoy his drinks whilst partying rather than getting serious, Violet seems more detached than he is as Lee, as if Lee wanted to disconnect from the world through this persona. Violet seems more unaffected by others, more carefree, and more eccentric. He vainly also claims to be 3 years younger than he actually is, with his age given as 45 when he is actually 48. As Violet, his primary aim is to bring fame and renown to his corporation, Violet Systems, and to promote his personally designed line of combots.

When dressed as his alter-ego Violet, Lee has dyed purple hair and wears black sunglasses. His costumes are flamboyant and usually follow a purple color scheme.

entities.name: Wang Jinrei
entities.description:
Wang Jinrei (王驚雷 Wáng Jīngléi; Japanese: ワン・ジンレイ Wan Jinrei; It may be written with given name first as Jinrei Wang) is a character in the Tekken series of fighting games, first introduced in the original Tekken game. He returned in Tekken 2, Tekken 5, and Tekken 6, and also for the spin-off games, Tekken Tag Tournament and Tekken Tag Tournament 2.

Wang is an old man who has seen a lot in life. From the way Wang dresses and the way he speaks of jiang shi and other legends, staying in a Fujian Tulou, knowing about Mokujin in Tekken 6 and mentioning gods, he seems to hold traditions and legends in great esteem. He possibly left China during the start of the Mao era if not before. Wang seems to have the means to acquire a lot of information, such as about Alisa, Ogre's epitaph, or the Mishima Zaibatsu. He is also someone who seems to want more from life and to hold a bigger role, as evidenced by when Xiaoyu tells him he's being overly-dramatic and has watched too many Kung Fu movies, or when he reunites all the older men, in his Tekken Tag Tournament 2 ending, to tell them that he wants to be recognized and seen as a young stud. This does not stop him also complaining from time to time about his old age and failing health.

Wang bears many regrets. He mentions his negligence toward the Mishima Zaibatsu that allowed it to expand so much, and all through Tekken 5 he expresses similar regret. He regrets not having been able to save his friend Jinpachi from his son Heihachi, and regrets having been manipulated by Heihachi for so many years. Heihachi somehow manipulated him into believing Jinpachi was a threat, and even tells Wang: "I’ll be the one to stop him, once and for all!", indicating that he perhaps painted his usurping of Jinpachi before in a positive light to Wang. Wang's reply ("I won’t let you fool me again!") indicates he has no intention of falling for this twice. Once beaten by Wang, Heihachi somehow acts pitifully saying: "Wang Jinrei how can you?...", perhaps showing that Wang was someone gentler in his younger days who spoiled Heihachi in his youth.

Wang's belated confrontation of the Mishimas may come out of strong loyalty to his friends. On beating Heihachi in Tekken 5, he remarks "Why do I have to hurt my friends to do the right thing?" and when Jinpachi asks him to kill him, Wang once more says: "I will not harm my friend ever again!" Although Wang does accept to fight Jinpachi, he wishes there were another way, indicating that conflict that results in challenging his former allies is a great burden to him. Wang's dedication to loyalty is also evidenced in his treatment of Feng Wei. He understood that Feng beat his master in a fair fight, and he talked to Lei (who was to arrest Feng) about it, exonerating Feng from culpability.

entities.name: Wu Zihao
entities.description:
Wu Zihao (ウー・ズーハオ Ū Zūhao) is a minor, non-playable character in the Tekken series. He first appeared in Tekken 5 as the master of Feng Wei, whom he taught traditional Chinese martial arts.

Wu Zihao was a sifu of the God Fist Style Chinese Martial Arts. He had his own martial arts school in rural China, where he trained pupils of all ages. At some point, the 'Secrets of the God Fist' scrolls belonging to the school were stolen by the Mishima Zaibatsu.

Zihao was a renowed martial artist, known as the 'God Fist', a title that his pupil, Feng Wei, would later claim for himself. Zihao was also known for his martial arts philosophy, that preached that it is essential for one's heart to be in line with one's technique.

Among Zihao's pupils was one student who trained with them since childhood, Feng Wei. By the age of 20, Feng was the school's top student. His philosophy clashed with that of his master, and he desired to become the strongest at all costs. One day, Feng broke the school rules by fighting off school ground. Zihao reprimanded Feng, and Feng ended up killing his master.

entities.name: Yoshimitsu
entities.description:
Yoshimitsu is a ninja and the leader of the Manji Clan, a group that steals from people who profit from dishonest activities so that they can redistribute this wealth to the poor. He wields a possessed sword, the Cursed Blade Yoshimitsu, a demon-slaying weapon that thirsts for blood and drives its wielder to sate its hunger; Yoshimitsu does this by cutting down wicked people. He entered the first King of Iron Fist Tournament to act as a decoy while his subordinates stole the event’s operating funds (though the success of this operation is unknown).

Some time prior to the King of Iron Fist Tournament 2, Yoshimitsu broke into the Mishima Zaibatsu’s research and development labs to steal the secrets of a ‘perpetual engine’ they were developing. Yoshimitsu was discovered by security forces, and his left arm was irreparably wounded during the ensuing firefight. However, the perpetual engine’s developer, Doctor Bosconovitch, operated on Yoshimitsu, fitting him with a replacement robotic arm powered by the perpetual generator. Yoshimitsu was able to escape from the Mishima Zaibatsu labs and entered the King of Iron Fist Tournament 2 in hopes of being able to free his savior, Doctor Bosconovitch, from his captivity in the Mishima Zaibatsu labs.

Yoshimitsu succeeded in freeing Doctor Bosconovitch. In the years that followed, he provided funds to aid in Bosconovitch’s cold sleep research, which he was carrying out to preserve his daughter who had passed away, whilst continuing to aid the poor and impoverished elsewhere. One day, Yoshimitsu visited Bosconovitch and learned that he had contracted a mysterious pathological organism while working on the cold sleep machine. Bosconovitch told Yoshimitsu he needed blood from Ogre, a being that had emerged in Central America, in order to life. Indebted to Bosconovitch, Yoshimitsu entered the King of Iron Fist Tournament 3 in an attempt to source Ogre’s blood. Yoshimitsu apparently succeeded, as Bosconovitch’s illness resolved.

Yoshimitsu began to grow concerned about the Manji Clan’s capacity to help the many disadvantaged people they served, and entered the King of Iron Fist Tournament 4, envisioning a union between the Manji Clan and Mishima Zaibatsu wherein the latter’s wealth could be used to do far greater good. Though the union between the Manji Clan and Mishima Zaibatsu did not come to be, Yoshimitsu succeeded in breaking into the Zaibatsu’s vaults and stealing money from them. He also found a wounded Bryan Fury during this break-in, and took him to Doctor Bosconovitch.

entities.description:
Yue was available in the game Tekken (Mobile) before the mobile app closed.

Her special moves are a blend between Leo Kliesen and Ling Xiaoyu with a traditional fighting style based on Bajiquan. She is focused on punches, strikes, and elbows. Her kicks are fairly flexible, allowing her to almost go into a Phoenix Stance after kicking her opponent. Some other strikes and elbowing also resemble that of Jaycee.

She uses the traditional Chinese Martial Arts (中國武術 Zhōngguó wǔshù) as some of her moves are based on Bajiquan.

entities.name: Zafina
entities.description:
Zafina (Arabic: زافينا Zāfīnā, Japanese: ザフィーナ Zafīna) is a playable character in the Tekken series. She is an astrologist whose village was tasked with protecting the tomb of Azazel.

Zafina was introduced in Tekken 6 and also appears in Tekken 7 as a DLC character in the third season pass, Tekken 8, and the spin off game Tekken Tag Tournament 2.

Zafina was born somewhere in the Middle East to a group of spiritual warriors with an ancient past and, as such, she possesses great spiritual abilities of her own.

From childhood, Zafina was raised to be a protector of an imperial tomb. Several years ago, a foreign army attacked the imperial tomb, and Zafina single-handedly wiped them out. Following that incident, the group’s guru appointed her to be the tomb's sole protector.

entities.name: Zombie Bride
entities.description:
Zombie Bride is a scrapped Tekken character.

The idea of the first fighting zombie in a game first came up during the development of Tekken 3, but since the fighting style for a zombie would be quite difficult to create, the idea was scrapped.

The idea resurfaced for Tekken 6, the character being the dead sister of Miguel Caballero Rojo who came back as a zombie and would fight in her tattered wedding gown; however, the idea was never approved nor elaborated upon.

The concept was once again reintroduced in Tekken Revolution when she became one of the candidates in Tekken Revolution's original character poll on the official Tekken Facebook page, where she was labelled as "Zombie Bride".

entities.name: Katsuhiro Harada
entities.description:
Harada was born in Osaka, Japan, and grew up in Nara Prefecture, the youngest of three children. He has two older sisters and his parents were civil servants. His parents saw him as the hope of the family, and to act as a role model, he was not allowed to play video games. Video games were, however, something that interested him. He often went to play his favorite video games in arcades.

He attended Waseda University in the late 1980s, along with Dead or Alive creator Tomonobu Itagaki. He holds a degree in psychology.

During this time, he spent most of his time playing video games and was convinced that his future lied there. He finds work in an arcade owned by Namco, located in Shinjuku in Tokyo. He mainly organized Street Fighter II tournaments. Through his studies in psychology, Harada studied the behavior of players in the arcade. He then made changes to the premises in order to observe the reactions of the people. He spoke with them and collected feedback. Namco's president at the time, commended Harada's work. Harada then encouraged Namco to work on producing video games for home consoles, having acquired some knowledge in that field. He later moved to Tokyo after completing his university studies there and eventually became a game designer.

Harada started as the advisory consultant of the first Tekken. For Harada, the fighting game needed to reach not only Japanese arcade players but also the general public, so that everyone could play it. Harada wanted Namco to make Tekken an console game for everyone. Although now, Harada somewhat regrets it because the game was not balanced enough (some characters were more powerful than others).

entities.name: Mishima Clan
entities.description:
The is one of the most important families in the Tekken series.

The Mishima family was originally a warrior clan that served the Japanese Emperor. The clan's origins date back to the Heian period (794 - 1185) during the time of the Taira and Minamoto clans, and the clan were celebrated for defeating demons and evil spirits. The family later capitalized on the outbreak of World War II and built an industrial empire that focused on providing militaristic resources to Japan.

After the war, Jinpachi Mishima started moving the focus of his corporation away from the military due to his growing distaste for unnecessary conflict, and instead focused more on martial arts training. He opened a personal dojo where he taught his own style of karate, the Mishima Style Fighting Karate. He taught both his son, Heihachi Mishima, and the young Kazumi, who was a member of the Hachijo Clan, a family of secret assassins that carried the Devil Gene in their blood.

Heihachi and Kazumi formed a lasting bond and the two fell in love over time. They married and had a son named Kazuya Mishima. Jinpachi was involved in the early training of his grandson, and the two had great affection for one another. After Jinpachi was imprisoned and Kazumi killed however, Heihachi was the sole teacher of Kazuya and his adopted son, Lee Chaolan, and was cruel and hard on them, teaching them by the motto: "A fight is about who is left standing. Nothing else".
